sessions.title: Welcome & What Even Is DevOps?
sessions.summary: Why DevOps exists, how a change travels from a laptop to a real user, and what we’ll build together this semester. No coding today — just the big picture.
topics: The 2 a.m. outage story: why “works on my machine” isn’t enough
Dev vs Ops: the wall, and how DevOps tears it down
From “I hit save” to “a user sees it”: mapping the journey
sessions.bring: Just yourself. If you don’t have a Google account yet, create one before next session — it’s all you’ll need all semester.

sessions.title: Meet the Command Line
sessions.summary: The terminal isn’t scary — it’s a remote control for computers. Open Cloud Shell in your browser and start giving commands.
topics: Moving around: pwd, ls, cd, mkdir
sessions.bring: A laptop with Chrome and a Google account. Everything runs in Cloud Shell — nothing to install.

sessions.title: Version Control Is Your Time Machine
sessions.summary: Why nobody emails final_v3_FINAL.zip anymore. Track every change to your work with Git and put it on GitHub.
topics: git init, add, commit and log
Pushing from Cloud Shell to GitHub
sessions.bring: A free GitHub account — create it before the session. Git is already installed in Cloud Shell.

sessions.title: Working Together Without Breaking Each Other’s Code
sessions.summary: Branches and pull requests let a whole team work on one codebase at once. We’ll cause a merge conflict on purpose — and fix it.
sessions.bring: Your GitHub account and last session’s repo. All in Cloud Shell and the browser.

sessions.title: What’s “The Cloud,” Really?
sessions.summary: You’re not renting a computer, you’re renting capacity. A guided tour of Google Cloud — we look around, we don’t spend anything.
topics: Regions, projects and the free tier
What you can do without a credit card
sessions.bring: Your Google account. No billing or credit card needed.

sessions.title: Cloud Shell: Your Free Dev Environment in a Browser
sessions.summary: A full Linux machine with every tool we’ll use this semester — free, in a browser tab. Learn the editor, Web Preview and gcloud.
topics: Web Preview: see a running app live
What persists between sessions (and what doesn’t)
sessions.bring: A laptop with Chrome. Read the Cloud Shell walkthrough on the blog first.

sessions.title: Serving Your First Website
sessions.summary: Your first URL that isn’t localhost. Build a small personal page in Cloud Shell and publish it for free with GitHub Pages.
topics: Previewing it live with Web Preview
Your name, a photo and your links
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell and your GitHub account. Free — no credit card.

sessions.title: Mini-Project Day: Ship Your Site
sessions.summary: Low-stakes demo-day energy. Finish your site, publish it, and share the live link.
topics: Commit, push, and watch it go live
sessions.bring: Your site repo from last session.

sessions.title: Why Containers?
sessions.summary: The shipping-container idea: pack an app with everything it needs so it runs the same anywhere. Concepts first, hands-on next session.
topics: Where you’ve already used containers without knowing
sessions.bring: Nothing extra.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Build Your First Container
sessions.summary: A Dockerfile is shorter than you think. Write one, build an image and run it — Docker is already in Cloud Shell.
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell (Docker is pre-installed) and your site repo. Nothing to install.

sessions.title: Running Containers in the Cloud
sessions.summary: Your container, but the internet can reach it. Watch a live deploy to Cloud Run, then run the same container yourself.
topics: What Cloud Run does for you
Live demo: deploying to Cloud Run
Running it yourself in Cloud Shell
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell. Public deploys need a billing-enabled project, so the deploy is a live demo on the club project — you follow along in Cloud Shell, no card needed.

sessions.title: Mini-Project: Containerise a Small App
sessions.summary: Bring a small idea — a to-do list, a joke API, anything — and ship it as a container, with mentors on hand.
topics: Run and test it in Cloud Shell
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell, GitHub and an idea. Starter templates will be provided.

sessions.title: What Is CI/CD, and Why Should You Care?
sessions.summary: A deploy that took four hours by hand versus four minutes automated. See the pipeline before you build one.
topics: A tour of a real pipeline
sessions.bring: Nothing extra.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Your First GitHub Actions Pipeline
sessions.summary: Automation that watches your repo for you. Write a workflow that runs on every push and earn your first green checkmark.
sessions.bring: Your Session 12 repo. GitHub Actions is free for public repos and runs on GitHub’s machines, not yours.

sessions.title: Deployment Strategies, Part 1: Rollbacks
sessions.summary: “We shipped a bug” isn’t a crisis if you planned for it. Break a release on purpose, then undo it.
topics: Why roll back first, fix second
Versioned images: tags as save points
Hands-on: roll back a container in Cloud Shell
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell. Read the Rollbacks post on the blog first.

sessions.title: Deployment Strategies, Part 2: Blue-Green & Multi-Region
sessions.summary: How big apps ship without anyone noticing. Watch a live blue-green flip and unpack how one app can run different versions in different regions.
topics: Live demo: splitting traffic between versions
One app, different versions per region
sessions.bring: Read the Blue-Green and Multi-Region posts on the blog first.

sessions.title: Observability 101: How Do You Know It’s Actually Broken?
sessions.summary: Logs are the check-engine light for software. Learn to find out something’s broken before a user tells you.
topics: Logs, metrics and alerts in plain English
Reading container logs in Cloud Shell
sessions.bring: Your Session 12 app and repo, in Cloud Shell.

sessions.title: Capstone Kickoff
sessions.summary: Teams of two or three, one small idea, shippable by 3 December. Scope it, set up the repo, start building.
topics: Scoping: what’s the smallest version worth demoing?
sessions.bring: Your team and your idea.

sessions.title: Capstone Work Session
sessions.summary: Mentor-supported build time. Build, debug, ask for help.
sessions.bring: Your team’s capstone repo.

sessions.title: Demo Day & Send-Off
sessions.summary: Show what you built. Each team demos live, then we break for exams — Semester 2 picks up in January.
topics: Keep going over the break with the LMS
sessions.bring: Your demo, ready to run.

sessions.title: Welcome Back & Raising the Bar
sessions.summary: What Semester 2 adds, and why it’s fine if it feels harder. Warm up by rebuilding a Semester 1 project from memory.
topics: Warm-up: rebuild a Semester 1 project without notes
Setting up your cloud project for this semester
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell and your Semester 1 repos. Several sessions this semester create real cloud resources — use a billing-enabled project or the club’s shared one.

sessions.title: Why “Click-Ops” Doesn’t Scale
sessions.summary: Clicking through a console fifty times is how typos become outages. Meet Infrastructure as Code.
sessions.bring: Nothing extra.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Your First Terraform Resource
sessions.summary: Describe one real piece of infrastructure in a text file, then create it with a single command.
topics: Reading a plan before you apply it
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell (Terraform is pre-installed) and a billing-enabled project.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Terraform for a Real Mini-Stack
sessions.summary: One resource is a demo; several working together is infrastructure. Provision a storage bucket and a Cloud Run service together.
sessions.bring: Last session’s Terraform repo.

sessions.title: Mini-Project: Rebuild Your Semester 1 App as Code
sessions.summary: Delete it, then bring it back with one command — the whole pitch for Infrastructure as Code, felt first-hand.
sessions.bring: Your Semester 1 app and your Terraform repo.

sessions.title: Why Containers Alone Aren’t Enough
sessions.summary: One container is easy. Fifty that must talk to each other, scale and heal themselves need an orchestrator.
topics: Clusters, nodes and the control plane
sessions.bring: Nothing extra.

sessions.title: Kubernetes Core Concepts
sessions.summary: Pods, Deployments and Services, demystified with analogies instead of jargon — then your first look at a real cluster.
sessions.bring: Cloud Shell (kubectl is pre-installed). A practice cluster will be provided.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Deploy Your App to Kubernetes
sessions.summary: The same container you built in Semester 1, in a new home. Write a manifest, apply it, see it run.
sessions.bring: Your Semester 1 container image and the practice cluster.

sessions.title: Self-Healing Systems: Kill a Pod, Watch It Come Back
sessions.summary: The Chaos Monkey idea, made real. Delete a running pod on purpose and watch Kubernetes replace it.
sessions.bring: Your running deployment. Read the Chaos Engineering post on the blog first.

sessions.title: Scaling in Kubernetes
sessions.summary: The Black Friday story, made real. Scale from one replica to five with a single command.
sessions.bring: Your running deployment. Read the Autoscaling post on the blog first.

sessions.title: Observability, For Real This Time
sessions.summary: Semester 1 looked at logs once. Now: logs, metrics and traces as a real practice.
topics: The three pillars: logs, metrics, traces
sessions.bring: A deployed app from Phase 1 or 2.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Build a Dashboard and an Alert
sessions.summary: The difference between hearing about an outage from a user and hearing about it first.
sessions.bring: Your deployed app.

sessions.title: DevOps Security 101: Secrets & Least-Privilege Access
sessions.summary: Most real breaches aren’t genius hackers — they’re a password pushed to GitHub by accident.
topics: A staged example of a leaked key
sessions.bring: Nothing extra.

sessions.title: Hands-On: Stop Hardcoding Secrets
sessions.summary: Move a real secret out of your code and into Secret Manager.
topics: Creating a secret in Secret Manager
Granting only the access that’s needed
Reading the secret from your app
Scrubbing a secret from Git history
sessions.bring: Your deployed app and its repo.

sessions.title: Canary Releases & Feature Flags, For Real This Time
sessions.summary: Semester 1 talked about testing on a slice of users — now you’ll actually do it.
topics: When to roll forward vs roll back
sessions.bring: Your deployed app.

sessions.title: GitOps: Deploying by Merging, Not by Typing Commands
sessions.summary: The best deploy command is the one you never type. Make merging to main the deploy.
topics: Git as the source of truth
Drift, and how GitOps fixes it
sessions.bring: Your app repo and its GitHub Actions pipeline.

sessions.title: Capstone II Kickoff
sessions.summary: Bigger teams, bigger scope: one project that uses everything from this year.
topics: Scoping with IaC, containers, CI/CD and monitoring
sessions.bring: Your team and your idea.

sessions.title: Capstone Work Session
sessions.summary: Mentor-supported build time.
sessions.bring: Your team’s capstone repo.

sessions.title: Capstone Work Session + Debug Clinic
sessions.summary: The unglamorous part — and what real engineering work actually feels like.
sessions.bring: Your team’s capstone repo.

sessions.title: Grand Demo Day & Send-Off
sessions.summary: Two semesters of work, on stage. Semester 1 members are invited.
topics: Where next: open source, certifications, internships
sessions.bring: Your demo, ready to run.

sessions.title: Where From Here
sessions.summary: A buffer if anything slipped, or a career-focused wrap if nothing did.
topics: Turning this year’s work into a portfolio
sessions.bring: Your laptop and your GitHub profile.
